issues.description: The template's ray_sphere_intersect header declares a function taking three parameters (origin, dir, center), but the implementation (ray_sphere_intersect.cpp) and all callers (main.cpp) use a fourth parameter 'radius'. The solution repository's header shows the intended prototype with the radius parameter. This mismatch will cause compilation errors (call/declared-prototype disagreement) and confuse students about the correct function signature.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the template header ray_sphere_intersect.h so its prototype matches the implementation and callers by including the radius parameter (e.g. bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);). This matches the solution and resolves the compile-time signature mismatch while preserving the intended API.

issues.description: The function ray_sphere_intersect is declared in the template header without a radius parameter, but its implementation (in the template) and the solution header define a fourth parameter 'const float radius'. This mismatch means the same conceptual entity (sphere-intersection test) is referenced with inconsistent function signatures across artifacts, causing compilation/runtime confusion and making it unclear to students which prototype to use.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template header prototype match the implementation and the solution: change the declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h to include the radius parameter. For example: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); This will align header and implementation and remove student confusion/compilation errors.
